cards.math: f=∑p∈{18,21,24}(x−p)2f=\sum_{p\in\{18,21,24\}}(x-p)^2f=∑p∈{18,21,24}​(x−p)2

cards.prompt: Thermostat preferences 18,21,24. Which derivative is right?
cards.explain: Each of the three squared terms contributes 2(x−preference).

cards.math: f′=2(x−18)+2(x−21)+2(x−24)f\prime=2(x-18)+2(x-21)+2(x-24)f′=2(x−18)+2(x−21)+2(x−24)

cards.prompt: Thermostat at 25: the official derivative is 6x−126. Gradient?
cards.explain: Use the current setting in the derivative.
cards.source: HW5 P3(ii) & P4, key pp.6–9; site lessons 8,10
cards.math: f′(25)=150−126=24f\prime(25)=150-126=24f′(25)=150−126=24

cards.prompt: Thermostat: x=25, gradient=24, η=0.1. Next setting?
cards.explain: The step subtracts 2.4; it approaches the optimum without reaching it.

cards.math: x1=25−0.1(24)=22.6x_1=25-0.1(24)=22.6x1​=25−0.1(24)=22.6

cards.prompt: Best thermostat setting for preferences 18,21,24?
cards.explain: Squared disagreement is minimized at their average.
cards.source: HW5 P3(ii) & P4, key pp.6–9; site lessons 8,10
cards.math: x∗=18+21+243=21x^*=\frac{18+21+24}{3}=21x∗=318+21+24​=21

cards.prompt: At thermostat optimum 21, are all roommates’ squared errors zero?
cards.explain: The best compromise still has errors −3,0,3; minimum loss is 18.
cards.source: HW5 P3(ii) & P4, key pp.6–9; site lessons 8,10
cards.math: f(21)=9+0+9=18f(21)=9+0+9=18f(21)=9+0+9=18

cards.prompt: Robot p=[6,2], q=[0,4]. Its gradient is…
cards.explain: Add both squared-distance gradients.
cards.source: HW5 P3(ii) & P4, key pp.6–9; site lessons 8,10
cards.math: 2(w−p)+2(w−q)=4w−2(p+q)2(w-p)+2(w-q)=4w-2(p+q)2(w−p)+2(w−q)=4w−2(p+q)

cards.prompt: Robot gradient is 4w−[12,12]. At w=[1,1], first entry?
cards.explain: Each entry is 4−12.
cards.source: HW5 P3(ii) & P4, key pp.6–9; site lessons 8,10
cards.math: g=[−8,−8]⊤g=[-8,-8]^\topg=[−8,−8]⊤

cards.prompt: Robot old gradient is [−8,−8]. Downhill direction?
cards.explain: Negate the gradient. Starting at [1,1], this points northeast toward the midpoint.
cards.source: HW5 P3(ii) & P4, key pp.6–9; site lessons 8,10
cards.math: −∇f=[8,8]⊤-\nabla f=[8,8]^\top−∇f=[8,8]⊤

cards.explain: Each coordinate adds 0.8.
cards.source: HW5 P3(ii) & P4, key pp.6–9; site lessons 8,10
cards.math: 1−.1(−8)=1.81-.1(-8)=1.81−.1(−8)=1.8

cards.prompt: Robot’s optimum between p=[6,2] and q=[0,4]?
cards.explain: The sum of squared distances is minimized at the midpoint.
cards.source: HW5 P3(ii) & P4, key pp.6–9; site lessons 8,10
cards.math: w∗=(p+q)/2w^*=(p+q)/2w∗=(p+q)/2

cards.prompt: From [1,1], downhill direction [8,8]; desired displacement [2,2]. One-step η?
cards.explain: One quarter of the direction vector is the required displacement.
cards.source: HW5 P3(ii) & P4, key pp.6–9; site lessons 8,10
cards.math: η=2/8=1/4\eta=2/8=1/4η=2/8=1/4

cards.prompt: Robot loss goes 36 → 25.76 after its .1 step. Is it already minimal?
cards.explain: One improving step need not solve the optimization problem.
cards.source: HW5 P3(ii) & P4, key pp.6–9; site lessons 8,10
cards.math: f(w∗)=20f(w^*)=20f(w∗)=20

cards.prompt: Toy f(w)=(w−3)²: start 0, η=.25. First new w?
cards.explain: The current gradient is −6, so add 1.5.
cards.source: Site lesson 10; original bowl
cards.math: 0−.25(−6)=1.50-.25(-6)=1.50−.25(−6)=1.5

cards.prompt: Same bowl: after reaching 1.5, reuse old gradient −6?
cards.explain: The new slope is 2(1.5−3)=−3.
cards.source: Site lesson 10
cards.math: gnew=2(wnew−3)g_{new}=2(w_{new}-3)gnew​=2(wnew​−3)

cards.prompt: Toy bowl with η=.25: 0 → 1.5 → 2.25. Next w?
cards.explain: Each step halves the remaining distance to 3.
cards.source: Site lesson 10; original mental pattern
cards.math: wnew=w+.5(3−w)w_{new}=w+.5(3-w)wnew​=w+.5(3−w)

cards.prompt: For (w−3)², η=1 and start 0 gives…
cards.explain: This step size preserves error magnitude instead of converging.
cards.source: Site lesson 11
cards.math: ek+1=(1−2η)eke_{k+1}=(1-2\eta)e_kek+1​=(1−2η)ek​

cards.prompt: For (w−3)², which η reaches 3 in one step?
cards.explain: Here the error multiplier becomes zero. This value is specific to this loss.
cards.source: Site lesson 11
cards.math: 1−2η=01-2\eta=01−2η=0

cards.prompt: For (w−3)², η=.75 gives…
cards.explain: Its error multiplier is −.5: signs alternate while magnitude halves.
cards.source: Site lesson 11
cards.math: ek+1=(1−2η)eke_{k+1}=(1-2\eta)e_kek+1​=(1−2η)ek​

cards.prompt: Making a learning rate larger always makes GD converge faster. True or false?
cards.explain: Too large a step can overshoot, oscillate or diverge.
cards.source: Site lesson 11
cards.math: wk+1=wk−η∇f(wk)w_{k+1}=w_k-\eta\nabla f(w_k)wk+1​=wk​−η∇f(wk​)

cards.prompt: Gradient is zero. The next ordinary GD update…
cards.explain: An ordinary update has zero displacement; it does not check the shape.
cards.source: Site lessons 10–11
cards.math: Δw=−η 0=0\Delta w=-\eta\,0=0Δw=−η0=0

cards.prompt: A differentiable convex loss has zero gradient. That point is…
cards.explain: For convex losses, the stationary-point condition is sufficient.
cards.source: Site lesson 11
cards.math: ∇f(w∗)=0(convex f)\nabla f(w^*)=0\quad\text{(convex }f\text{)}∇f(w∗)=0(convex f)

cards.prompt: Different starts find different minima of a nonconvex loss. Restarts prove the global best?
cards.explain: Restarts may help, but do not certify a global optimum.
cards.source: Site lesson 11
cards.math: local minimum≠guaranteed global minimum\text{local minimum}\ne\text{guaranteed global minimum}local minimum=guaranteed global minimum

cards.prompt: Switch SSE to MSE on N samples. To preserve the same GD step, η should…
cards.explain: MSE divides the gradient by N, so compensate with the learning rate.
cards.source: Site lessons 12,14
cards.math: ∇MSE=∇SSE/N\nabla MSE=\nabla SSE/N∇MSE=∇SSE/N

cards.prompt: Multiply a loss by 10. To keep the same GD displacement, step size should…
cards.explain: The gradient is ten times larger, but the minimizers are unchanged.
cards.source: Site lesson 14
cards.math: ∇(10f)=10∇f\nabla(10f)=10\nabla f∇(10f)=10∇f

cards.prompt: MSE gradient (2/N)Xᵀ(Xc−y) uses which residual sign?

cards.source: Site lesson 12
cards.math: ∇L=−2NX⊤e\nabla L=-\frac2N X^\top e∇L=−N2​X⊤e

cards.prompt: Least-squares normal equations and zero MSE gradient describe…
cards.explain: For this convex quadratic, both solve XᵀXc=Xᵀy.
cards.source: Site lesson 12
cards.math: X⊤(Xc−y)=0X^\top(Xc-y)=0X⊤(Xc−y)=0

cards.prompt: For f(w)=‖w−b‖²+a·w, the optimum is…

cards.math: w∗=b−a/2w^*=b-a/2w∗=b−a/2

cards.prompt: Two equal folds have MSEs 1.7 and 1.0. Final CV MSE?
cards.explain: Average the two equal-sized fold MSEs into one final number.
cards.source: Full site lesson 13; Quiz 4 learning-target repair
cards.math: CV MSE=(1.7+1.0)/2CV\ MSE=(1.7+1.0)/2CV MSE=(1.7+1.0)/2

cards.prompt: Two equal folds have MSEs 1 and 3. Final CV MSE?
cards.explain: The sum 4 is an intermediate result; divide by two folds.
cards.source: Full site lesson 13; Quiz 4 learning-target repair; smaller original example
cards.math: (1+3)/2=2(1+3)/2=2(1+3)/2=2

cards.prompt: A 1-case fold has MSE 1; a 3-case fold has MSE 3. Overall per-case MSE?
cards.explain: Weight by held-out sample counts: (1×1+3×3)/4.
cards.source: Full site lesson 13; Quiz 4 learning-target repair; original unequal-fold example
cards.math: MSE=∑nkMSEk∑nkMSE=\frac{\sum n_k MSE_k}{\sum n_k}MSE=∑nk​∑nk​MSEk​​

cards.prompt: Ten samples: degree 2 CV R²=.96; degree 3=.97. Preferred course choice?
cards.explain: A .01 difference on tiny data is not persuasive; prefer the simpler near-top model.
cards.source: Full site lesson 13; Quiz 4 learning-target repair
cards.math: near-tied held-out performance⇒simpler model\text{near-tied held-out performance}\Rightarrow\text{simpler model}near-tied held-out performance⇒simpler model

cards.prompt: Why not select polynomial degree using the highest training R²?
cards.explain: A larger model can reproduce a smaller one, improving training fit without better future predictions.
cards.source: Full site lesson 13; Quiz 4 learning-target repair
cards.math: choose using held-out predictions\text{choose using held-out predictions}choose using held-out predictions

cards.source: Full site lesson 13; Quiz 4 learning-target repair
cards.math: hide→fit→test→choose→refit\text{hide}\to\text{fit}\to\text{test}\to\text{choose}\to\text{refit}hide→fit→test→choose→refit

cards.explain: Add true flags and all flags. Do not average ratios with unequal denominators.
cards.source: Full site lesson 13; Quiz 4 learning-target repair
cards.math: PPVpooled=1+92+10PPV_{pooled}=\frac{1+9}{2+10}PPVpooled​=2+101+9​

cards.math: x⊤x=1+4+9=14x^\top x=1+4+9=14x⊤x=1+4+9=14

cards.explain: Equality is included.

cards.explain: Among actual positives, count those caught.
cards.source: Instructor formula sheet transcribed in site lesson 16; HW5 key
cards.math: TPR=TPTP+FNTPR=\frac{TP}{TP+FN}TPR=TP+FNTP​

cards.explain: Among actual negatives, count false alarms.
cards.source: Instructor formula sheet transcribed in site lesson 16; HW5 key
cards.math: FPR=FPFP+TNFPR=\frac{FP}{FP+TN}FPR=FP+TNFP​

cards.prompt: ROC axes and AUC?
cards.answer: Horizontal FPR; vertical TPR; area under curve
cards.explain: For segments, use width times average height.

cards.prompt: Gradient descent update?
cards.answer: Old parameters minus η times old gradient

cards.explain: A linear function has constant coordinate slopes.

cards.explain: Apply the power rule to each coordinate.

cards.math: ∇w∥w∥2=2w\nabla_w\|w\|^2=2w∇w​∥w∥2=2w

cards.math: ∥v∥2=v⋅v=∑jvj2\|v\|^2=v\cdot v=\sum_jv_j^2∥v∥2=v⋅v=∑j​vj2​

cards.prompt: Prior formula?
cards.explain: Recall from memory; not printed in the supplied image.
cards.source: Instructor formula sheet transcribed in site lesson 16; HW5 key
cards.math: π=TP+FNN\pi=\frac{TP+FN}{N}π=NTP+FN​

cards.prompt: Accuracy formula?
cards.explain: Recall from memory; both kinds of correct predictions count.
cards.source: Instructor formula sheet transcribed in site lesson 16; HW5 key
cards.math: Acc=TP+TNNAcc=\frac{TP+TN}{N}Acc=NTP+TN​

cards.prompt: Precision / PPV formula?
cards.explain: Recall from memory; the denominator is all positive predictions.
cards.source: Instructor formula sheet transcribed in site lesson 16; HW5 key
cards.math: PPV=TPTP+FPPPV=\frac{TP}{TP+FP}PPV=TP+FPTP​

cards.explain: Derive by the chain rule from the squared norm.

cards.math: ∇w∥w−p∥2=2(w−p)\nabla_w\|w-p\|^2=2(w-p)∇w​∥w−p∥2=2(w−p)

cards.explain: This is a site extension connecting last week to gradients.

cards.math: ∇L=2NX⊤(Xc−y)\nabla L=\frac2N X^\top(Xc-y)∇L=N2​X⊤(Xc−y)

cards.prompt: Bank 2: 5 missed frauds at $500 each, 180 flags at $5 each. Total daily cost?
cards.explain: Add missed-fraud cost and the cost of every flag, including true positives.

cards.math: FPR=1515+165=112FPR=\frac{15}{15+165}=\frac1{12}FPR=15+16515​=121​

cards.math: AUC=.0625+.1875+.21875+.25AUC=.0625+.1875+.21875+.25AUC=.0625+.1875+.21875+.25
